description: Stable, schema-backed registry of ALL agent-facing reason labels: the hard runtime blocker codes consumed by coordinator preflight (workspace_coordination_preflight), MCP dispatch (workspace_agent_dispatch), and launcher diagnostics, AND self-recoverable agent-facing nudge labels (e.g. the read_disclosure compact-read gate refusals) whose recovery is the caller re-calling with corrected arguments. This file is the sole canonical source of truth for the taxonomy: dispatch-specific consumers, launcher diagnostics, and the compact-read gate MUST select codes from this descriptor rather than inventing ad hoc strings. Codes are dimensioned by category and actor_recovery so a self-fixable nudge and a hard block can coexist in one enumerable list without a consumer mistaking one for the other; dispatch-facing projections filter to the dispatch/launch categories so nudge labels do not leak into the dispatch blocker catalog. BOOTSTRAP_STATE_CODES values are string-equal to the bootstrap entries below.

private_cause_declarations.reason: Launcher transition plans carry imperative PRIVATE action tokens. They are flat snake_case and therefore indistinguishable by grammar from a public mechanical code, which is exactly how an uncallable token reaches an agent as if it were a route. They are declared here so the registry can refuse them by NAME, and they are deliberately not registered as codes.

Launcher-private transition causes. WK-2388 owns the classification that consumes them and requires that they stay unpublished: such a cause may select an existing mechanical transition tuple, but exposing it merely to classify the transition is refused. Registering one here would publish it as a public mechanical identity, so a private cause is NOT registered merely because it exists.

non_registrable_authority_identities.description: Identities owned by an external authority rather than by this local mechanical registry. They are transported verbatim inside an authenticated carrier and are never registered as local public mechanical codes, because registering one would give a local module a semantic opinion about a decision it did not make.

graph_impact_state_map.description: Exhaustive deterministic mapping from (graph_state, staleness, dirty_state, overlay_state) to the graph-impact evidence disposition consumed by workspace_coordination_preflight and workspace_agent_dispatch readiness. The first matching rule wins. A null/unspecified field matches any value. A rule's blocking and outcome are its dispatch disposition; the named code stays a registered identity for genuine explicit graph-query failures. Graph-impact evidence is supplementary to dispatch (DEC-0177; WK-2613 entry 2): no graph state refuses dispatch or preflight. The baseline is derived from the current committed HEAD, so a stale, older-base, missing-overlay, or rebuild_required state is rebuilt there. A current-HEAD baseline that cannot be produced or validated (graph_state unavailable/error/query_error) is reported as proceed_without_graph_evidence: dispatch continues and that state is never consumed as graph coverage. A valid dirty-worktree overlay is optional enrichment merged over the base (non-blocking graph_impact_degraded_overlay).
